descriptors.disclaimer: CEN and CENELEC neither endorse nor have reviewed this mapping. A verdict here is a projection of this assessment that supports the manufacturer's technical documentation; it is not a presumption of conformity: the sections of each standard named "rationale" and "guidance" confer none (Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/138), and a control marked Restricted carries the further restriction named on it. Scope of this version: EN 18031-1 (Article 3(3)(d)) and EN 18031-2 (Article 3(3)(e)) for internet-connected radio equipment. EN 18031-3 (Article 3(3)(f), equipment that transfers money, monetary value or virtual currency) is out of scope; such equipment needs a separate assessment. Within EN 18031-2, only equipment processing personal data is judged; the toy, childcare and wearable clauses, and traffic and location data, are out of scope because the questionnaire does not ask about them. Applicability is decided by the answers: QA5 (wireless connections) with QA6 or QA10b (internet connection) for Part 1, and QI2 (personal data) in addition for Part 2. QA5 asks about wireless connections more broadly than radio equipment, so the product's radio role decides whether this framework applies. Each requirement shows the EN IEC 62443-4-2:2019 requirements its part's informative Annex B names; these links are shown and never change a verdict. It applies to radio equipment placed on the market between 1 August 2025 and 10 December 2027; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 is repealed with effect from 11 December 2027 (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/339).

Annex I, Part II: vulnerability handling requirements

identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in products with digital elements, including by drawing up a software bill of materials in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at the very least the top-level dependencies of the products;
controls.notes: Maintain a component inventory and a machine-readable SBOM (e.g. CycloneDX or SPDX) covering at least top-level dependencies, regenerated for every release.

controls.title: in relation to the risks posed to products with digital elements, address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including by providing security updates; where technically feasible, new security updates shall be provided separately from functionality updates;
controls.notes: Operate a remediation process with defined timelines; ship security fixes decoupled from feature releases where technically feasible.

controls.title: apply effective and regular tests and reviews of the security of the product with digital elements;
controls.notes: Establish a recurring security testing cadence (e.g. penetration tests, fuzzing, dependency scanning, code review) and record the results.

controls.title: once a security update has been made available, share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities, including a description of the vulnerabilities, information allowing users to identify the product with digital elements affected, the impacts of the vulnerabilities, their severity and clear and accessible information helping users to remediate the vulnerabilities; in duly justified cases, where manufacturers consider the security risks of publication to outweigh the security benefits, they may delay making public information regarding a fixed vulnerability until after users have been given the possibility to apply the relevant patch;
controls.notes: Publish security advisories per fixed vulnerability: description, affected versions, impact, severity, and remediation steps. Delayed publication must be justified and time-bounded.

controls.title: put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure;
controls.notes: Adopt, publish and enforce a CVD policy (e.g. based on ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111).

controls.title: take measures to facilitate the sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities in their product with digital elements as well as in third-party components contained in that product, including by providing a contact address for the reporting of the vulnerabilities discovered in the product with digital elements;
controls.notes: Provide a single, published point of contact (e.g. security@ address and security.txt) for vulnerability reports, covering third-party components.

controls.title: provide for mechanisms to securely distribute updates for products with digital elements to ensure that vulnerabilities are fixed or mitigated in a timely manner and, where applicable for security updates, in an automatic manner;
controls.notes: Protect the update channel end-to-end (signed updates, integrity and authenticity verification on device); support automatic security updates where applicable.

controls.title: ensure that, where security updates are available to address identified security issues, they are disseminated without delay and, unless otherwise agreed between a manufacturer and a business user in relation to a tailor-made product with digital elements, free of charge, accompanied by advisory messages providing users with the relevant information, including on potential action to be taken.
controls.notes: Distribute security updates promptly and free of charge for the committed support period, accompanied by advisories with recommended user actions.
